title: Are you going to "forget" to disclose AI usage to Steam?
author: HereToLearn321
selftext: Have any of you already "forgotten" to disclose? And how did it go? I see a few games without the AI disclosure that clearly have AI art. I myself have disclosed so far.  One big youtuber responded saying they don't cover games using AI art.

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: No, I will definitely disclose it and say it was made by AI. Pure AI haters are not my target audience anyway, I want people who care about quality of the game not about being salty online.

replies.author: devloper27
replies.body: Their money is kind of important though

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: Not for me, I'm making my project out of hobby not for financial gain. I will be honest I would love if my game earned me enough to be able to keep putting 300$ a month into AI to make the game (those are approximately my costs of making my game), but even if it doesn't I initially didn't even hope for a single $. My goal was to push "AI made game" to the level of game some proper smaller studio would make.

replies.author: robogame_dev
replies.body: So is their consent?

replies.author: siberianmi
replies.body: Not for long.

comments.author: arjuna66671
comments.body: If I ever publish a vibecoded game on Steam I will absolutely disclose it - proudly so. Most anti-AI's you see online are a loud minority and they will vanish, one by one. In one or two years from now, no one will care if the game is actually any good.

replies.author: je386
replies.body: I guess that all studios use coding agents right now, and in 2 years even more so. Propably they have specialisied image generators, too.

replies.author: Burning_magic
replies.body:
Using AI to code and using AI to generate your models and art is 2 entirely different things. Even steam is explicitly ok with code.

Its only a big issue when people start using AI for key art and assets. People are not blind, any game that uses AI assets will be canned very fast. Whereas a game that uses AI code but humam assets will be largely indistinguishable from non AI games.

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: Just look up Call of Duty on Steam. They don’t even tell you what they use but boy are they using it. But the Indie devs that use AI get all the hate

comments.author: scotchable
comments.body: I have and will continue to do so, hell I've left it on mine that I use it for code even though we don't have to anymore.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: You want to get banned from Steam?

replies.author: Reasonable-Plum7059
replies.body: Source? Yall continue to spread this idea without source.

comments.author: ChemicalPresent8796
comments.body: Not forgetting it. On our deckbuilder the card art and the music are AI placeholders, and that is on the Steam page and in the trailer caption. The reason is boring: we cannot pay for human art yet, and pretending the placeholders are final would be worse than the disclosure. Code is a mix. The hard parts we write, a lot of the bulk is generated and then we fix it. I would rather say that than have someone find the Suno track later.

comments.author: TheReviewerWildTake
comments.body:
I would rather disclose, because quite frankly, I wouldn\`t want modern reddit-syle anti-AI cultists to be anywhere around me, and the best filter to achieve that, seems to be steam label.   
Otherwise you risk having those stupid discussions all the way through game\`s lifecycle.

replies.author: dont-pull-a-druckman
replies.body: It's a hard choice for me, cause I'd like for as many people to enjoy my games as much as possible, but no matter how little AI is used in the process, even if 99% of it is human made, you will get witch hunted by these anti AI people. Just sucks :(

replies.author: Psychological-Key-36
replies.body: Is your game actually 99% handmade?

replies.author: dont-pull-a-druckman
replies.body: I'd say like 80% human made? I do all the art and animation myself, just not the coding. But even then I pay programmers to look it over and check it. Just used 99% as an example of how I've seen projects which don't even use AI for the code aspect, but will use it for a small generative purpose like names or something, and their communities will absolutely lose their god damn minds.

replies.author: Psychological-Key-36
replies.body: If you’re doing all the art by yourself you should be fine. Your actual audience doesn’t care how the code is done. They want endearing or interesting graphics and a bugless experience

replies.author: LetsPlay2D
replies.body: ok so im an anti and using ai as an actual tool where you look over what the ai does is completely fine in my book. the problem starts when you stop doing that and ai goes rampart in the code. my two cents. you're good. (i would kinda make sure the programmers know what they are doing and not accept everything no matter what lol)

replies.author: dont-pull-a-druckman
replies.body:
Reassuring to hear that. Yeah if I could pay to have real programmers do the entire thing I would, but unfortunately low income. I also like being able to draft stuff up without needing to pay someone for multiple revisions, and I can spend my own time making something the way I want, and a professional can go through and vet it for slop. 

It's so sad to see so many people on this sub butchering their games with the most ugly uninspired assets imaginable. They either make it an ugly low poly flat colored & flat shaded 3D game, or they make it an overly detailed AI-generated pixel art looking mess. I just don't get it.

The unfortunate thing about these amazing tools is it makes every "ideas guy" think he's hot shit, and they act shocked when people don't like their dogshit lol.

replies.author: LetsPlay2D
replies.body: I did not mean to say you cant use AI for professional programming, thats not my point, just fact check everything it does, so it doesnt just add things you do not want! :) using AI as a tool to help is good and speeds things up, even if i never do that, lol.

replies.author: dont-pull-a-druckman
replies.body: Oh I didn't take it that way, I wasn't upset lol. The first part of my last comment wasn't typed to sound snarky

replies.author: KhaosPT
replies.body: The steam label doesn't make sense if ai is doing code. There is not a single studio that is coding stuff by hand only, the AI is just a too good productivity multiplier. Next year no one will care. I personally would not disclose that you used ai to code, it's irrelevant to the end user.

replies.author: glimsky
replies.body: You don't have to disclose AI coding unless the code itself uses AI to generate content on the fly.

comments.author: Electronic_Start_694
comments.body:
Where are they going to draw the line?  Realistically in no time flat, literally every single game that you'd want to play would carry this branding.  Are they going to break it down by time, and method?

All AAA houses are using AI in some capacity.

replies.author: BanjoThunderbird
replies.body: The line is basically that AI-generated code can be undisclosed but nothing else, so your concern isn't really valid.

replies.author: karl_mainz
replies.body: The big studios use AI to help generate assets too - but they’ll outsource the asset generation to a third party. And the third party has to deliver a lot at the lowest price possible, but sure, no AI 😉

replies.author: BanjoThunderbird
replies.body:
Sure but that's a different point right? If a company isn't disclosing properly then that should get chased up.   
  
That doesn't change the validity of disclosure, IMO it's not going to become redundant because every studio is generating content. If the line was at code, then sure, but there's going to be a lot of small studios that maintain a no generated content policy purely to cater to the haters market.

replies.author: karl_mainz
replies.body:
Because technically they aren't lying - they have plausible deniability.

The developer can say they had no idea that AI was being used by the third party studio.

replies.author: BanjoThunderbird
replies.body: Sure, in that case they just have to update their disclosure. But again, how does this make disclosure redundant? There are tons of anti AI studios that aren't triple A, just because some big names could cheat the system, doesn't mean the label is useless.

replies.author: BanjoThunderbird
replies.body: Yeah that's a good point, gambling on having to update their disclosure is a good price for a triple A. But again, how does this make disclosure redundant? There are tons of anti AI studios that aren't triple A, just because some big names could cheat the system, doesn't mean the label is useless.

replies.author: karl_mainz
replies.body:
I think the only people who can't cheat the system are solo devs and extremely small teams.

For anyone bigger than that, it's pretty trivial as outsourcing certain stuff like music, bits of art etc. isn't uncommon anyway. 

Although to be honest even small teams can do it via stuff like Fiverr - if the dude who made a whole load of sprites for you for $50 says he didn't use AI then it's fine.

replies.author: BanjoThunderbird
replies.body: I really doubt many small/medium indie studios are going to be outsourcing work to people they don't trust like that, they lose way too much control. The dog shit you'd get back would be unusable. It would only work at the scale that big studios could afford.

replies.author: United_Ad6480
replies.body: All my assets are generated procedurally by code, so do I have to disclose that then?

replies.author: BanjoThunderbird
replies.body: Yes, I'd say something like "The assets were generated by AI-written code" in that case.

replies.author: siberianmi
replies.body:
The when code produces the content, how are you drawing that line?

We’ve seen dozens of asset free games posted here where Opus did every element even the sound in code.

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
If I will release on steam, too, I will disclose. But that is something for "next year, maybe".

At the moment, I am working on a major upgrade to get the game to be fun. This has to be finished before adding more platforms.
I have released on other platforms which do not need to disclose AI usage, and I hope that the whole Anti-AI will get less and less while AI usage becomes more and more widespread.

comments.author: Lextrot
comments.body: Won't have to, all the art will be redrawn in Mspaint. At least it will be Human-made.

comments.author: TonyZwilde
comments.body: My game is still far away to be released, but for now I am just using Codex to help with the code, no generated assets, so probably not if it stays that way

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body: No I'm just going to move to Epic.

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: ![gif](giphy|zbzNUbpFnlw8E)

comments.author: BanjoThunderbird
comments.body: I think disclosing gen AI used for anything but programming is the ethical thing to do. Whether or not you agree, there are tons of people who have valid concerns about AI use and they should be respected enough to not lie in their face. Take the high road, people will realize the potential in AI game development before long and no one will care.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: if you want ai assisted game dev to be taken serious don't hide it, people have problems if you do or don't, and the'y will have problems with something. youtbuers like drama and so does reddit really, people in real life for the most part don't even care

comments.author: StretchedNut
comments.body: I only use it for code so apparently I don’t need to disclose this

replies.author: fued
replies.body: Yeah it's insane how hypocritical it is

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: I think Steam has a very fair disclosure policy, and I would just be honest about it. There are also things that, if I ever release a game on Steam, I would have things like voice acting (I have some experience with coordinating voicework, and honestly, talented amateur to early professional voice actors is really not expensive), key art, and some sprite work human-made from the prototype. This is out of a genuine belief that certain things are just better with a human in the loop, but I also think that drawing a clear line on what I do consider AI-assistable and where I still would want human work is at least a defensible position.

replies.author: devloper27
replies.body: For an indie dev everything is expensive

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body: Of course, not everyone has the same amount of money available, I didn't mean to imply that. But I'm an indie developer as well and for a game I really think has potential, I'm willing and luckily able to put in 1500€-ish, which can actually get you quite a bit. My point is that certain things that do make a game more human are no longer "you need a budget of a million" issues but "only slightly more expensive than the GenAI subscription you're already paying" issues.

comments.author: Victorex123
comments.body: If you want to be labeled as a liar go ahead.

comments.author: Brief_Shopping2222
comments.body: None of this will matter in 10 years. Same thing happened when Photoshop and digital art tools replaced model shops and illustration artists. Redditors happily consume that slop with no question.

comments.author: Interesting-Yellow-4
comments.body: I disclosed, got like 60 wishlists.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body: I'd rather just disclose the info. Some anti-Ai people might not play my games and I'm alright with it. I'm just happy to be making my dream games.

comments.author: MotivatedforGames
comments.body: "There is nothing well-documented case of Valve permanently banning an already-released game solely because the developer forgot to disclose generative-AI use" umm

comments.author: standardofiron
comments.body: I disclosed it, https://store.steampowered.com/app/5129960/Standard\_of\_Iron/

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
I would disclose. The more good games gonna have AI disclosed - the warmer an audience will be toward future AI peojects. And besides, some youtubers do play AI games. There will be more of them
. Lying is a quick cash grab, and being honest is investment into a better future

comments.author: MrDentifrice
comments.body: If you wanna use or defend AI then ok but disclose it.

comments.author: Reasonable-Plum7059
comments.body: No. Disclosing doesn’t not make anything better except for antis to spread hate. Content of game matters not the how game is made.

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: People will hate on your AI usage even tho you only generated one picture for your game. I will disclose it, but I will not hold back and use AI for anything tbh

comments.author: Wiskersthefif
comments.body: Ohhh, you really should disclose. You should see  the tos stuff about what happens if you're caught, because you will get caught and you'll really, really wish you'd just disclosed.

replies.author: leodennis2
replies.body: Well you don't need to and should not disclose AI coding. Only stuff that is actually seen by the user that was generated with AIGen. Coding and Organizing with AI is allowed in General without disclosure, it's probably done by almost everyone now anyways.

replies.author: siberianmi
replies.body:
And if every game asset is simply generated code?  Which is where we are now if you use the latest Anthropic models.

We are just going to end up in a place where essentially every title will have a disclosure.

replies.author: leodennis2
replies.body: Sooner or later almost everyone will use AI just like everyone uses other tools to develop things like Art but it might take a few years. I think what you mean is procedually generated graphics. Some feel like it does bot need disclosure because the AI only wrote the rules and mathematics how to build up an object. For very simple things that might be true (like add GPU optimized grass) but if the AI is building complex things and is assessing the locks and tweaking it then I surely argue it is AI generated that needs disclosure.

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
My biggest motivation for submitting to Steam/public is so that I can show off what AI is capable of, so absolutely going to center it/foreground it, not hide it! 

Claude is a character in the game, literally an architect of it - he's a haughty Frenchman who handles some tutorials.   
Astra is some kind of distant machine god spoken about in the lore only, they lit the stars of our universe. 

There's all kinds of interesting new narrative opportunities if you treat AI as actual co-authors, and the fourth wall as a glory hole. 

https://preview.redd.it/wi3km0ocntsh1.png?width=612&format=png&auto=webp&s=66e38b82541058989c25f96a1c1bdffbfb41c75c

comments.author: DJDerpTronic
comments.body: I should be launching a closed alpha in a couple weeks and Ill be disclosing. All my assets and animations are purchased to support creators. AI was only used for coding and hooking everything together. Based on Steams policy it probably wont be flagged but who knows.

comments.author: XXIIIOIIIXX
comments.body:
No. The game i'm working on will clearly state that I used AI for most of it because i'm not a gamedev, but some guy with a dream game stuck in his head for years and finally having the means to make it real.

Redditards dunking on common people making games with AI are like "master cooks" dunking on people making microwaved lasagna or something. Like, let me do my thing and f off somewhere else.

comments.author: Equal-Border-7793
comments.body: Whether it’s the art or the code, AI handles it all; for music, however, there isn't yet a good way to replace human input. I believe that what most people dislike is simply low-quality AI work, not the fact that the work was generated by AI itself—at least, the conflict between humans and AI hasn't reached that point yet.

comments.author: Seerix
comments.body: Be 100% honest with people or don't bother releasing a damn thing. You want the AI stigma to change? Release good games and be completely transparent about where and how Ai was used.

comments.author: HandshakeOfCO
comments.body:
I think Steam should add code for additional checkboxes that might help people decide whether to buy a game, like “was any part of the game created by a trans person” or “was any part of the game’s code written on a computer powered by coal?”

You see the problem with AI disclosure now, right? 

Real world issues exist and should be debated and paid attention to, but let’s call Steam’s checkbox what it really is: censorship.

comments.author: C0L0SSUSvdm
comments.body: Do you have to disclose vibe code? Ill let claude put placeholder art in but if its something trivial and insignificant that i could have made myself but it already looks exactly how id make it anyway i feel it's redundant and defeats the purpose somewhat to waste my time modeling the exact same thing just so i can replace the AI
